issue.title: Ignore all dunders when checking attributes in `sqlalchemy.util.langhelpers.TypingOnly`
issue.body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your proposed changes in the Title field above -->

Add missing Python 3.13 built-in attribute `__static_attributes__` in `sqlalchemy.utils.langhelpers.TypingOnly`.

### Description
<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->

An exception is raised on Python 3.13:

```
AssertionError: Class <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.SQLCoreOperations'> directly inherits TypingOnly but has additional attributes {'__static_attributes__'}.
```

This PR addresses it by adding the missing attribute to the check within `TypingOnly`.

Fixes #11334


### Checklist

SQLAlchemy v2.0.24 fails with Python 3.13 with error:
```
AssertionError: Class <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.SQLCoreOperations'> directly inherits TypingOnly but has additional attributes {'__static_attributes__'}.
```

body:
I had the similar issue `while importing below modules` in python3.13
```
from flask import Flask, render_template 
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey, Float
```

Error Message
`AssertionError: Class <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.SQLCoreOperations'> directly inherits TypingOnly but has additional attributes {'__firstlineno__', '__static_attributes__'}.`

**Fixed**
Fixed by creating a separate venv using python3.9, and it works in my case!
I think you had an old version of sqlalchemy in that env, both of those attributes match the regexp used `re.compile("^__.+__$")` so I don't see how you would get that error otherwise
Edgar Ramírez-Mondragón: I had the same issue with Python 3.13. Downgrade to Python 3.9 has solved the problem - for now. At some stage Heroku will force me to upgrade Python :-(
Have you tried updating sqlalchemy version instead?
Running Python v.3.13.2 and upgraded sqlalchemy to v.2.0.38 resolved this error for me. Thanks @CaselIT !

> I think you had an old version of sqlalchemy in that env, both of those attributes match the regexp used `re.compile("^__.+__$")` so I don't see how you would get that error otherwise

issue.body:
From Python 3.13 onwards, SQLAlchemy 2.0.6, which we currently run, throws this error:
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/11334
To avoid this becoming a problem, we should bump to at least 2.0.30, in which the bug is fixed.
